chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn Jazak from Yasir the servant, who said:

There were servants in the house of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who were Slavic and Roman. Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was close to them, so he heard them at night speaking in Slavic and Roman, saying: 'We used to donate blood once a year in our lands, but we have not donated blood here.' When it was the next day, Abu al-Hasan sent for some doctors and told them: 'Lance so-and-so's vein such-and-such, and lance so-and-so's vein such-and-such, and lance so-and-so's vein such-and-such, and lance this one's vein such-and-such.' Then he said: 'O Yasir, did you not donate blood?' I said: 'I donated blood, so my hand swelled and turned red.' He said to me: 'O Yasir, what is wrong with you?' I informed him. He said: 'Did I not forbid you from that? Bring your hand.' He wiped his hand over it and spat in it, then he instructed me not to eat dinner. I stayed for as long as God willed not eating dinner, then I would be negligent and eat dinner, so the pain would return upon me.
ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam al-Ridha and the bloodletting of his servants?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith highlights Imam al-Rida’s comprehensive knowledge (*‘ilm*) of foreign languages and medical practices, demonstrating his awareness of the specific cultural habits of his Slavic and Roman servants. The narrative further illustrates the practical application of this knowledge through the healing of Yasir’s hand, serving as a tangible sign of the Imam’s authority and a lesson in obedience to his specific instructions regarding diet and health.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 54-1 (The author of the book narrated) my father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jazak, on the authority of Yasir - the servant,

“There were servants in Abal Hassan Ar-Ridha’’s (a.s.) home who were Slavic and Roman. Abul Hassan’s (a.s.) room was near theirs. One night Imam Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) heard them say in the Slavic and Roman languages, ‘We used to donate blood once a year when we were in our own towns. However, we have never donated any blood for the many years that we have been here.’ Then when the morning came, Abal Hassan Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) called in some doctors and told them to take blood from each of those servants. He precisely instructed the doctors as to which of the veins to use for each of the servants. Then he (a.s.) told me, ‘O Yasir! You should not donate blood.’ However, I did not pay any attention to the Imam (a.s.) and donated blood. However, my hand swelled up and turned purple. Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) asked me, ‘What has happened to you?’ I answered, ‘I donated blood.” The Imam (a.s.) asked, ‘Did I not admonish you against donating blood? Please bring your hand forward.’ I put my hand forward. Then the Imam (a.s.) rubbed his hands on my hand and spit on it. Then the Imam (a.s.) ordered me not to eat dinner for a while. I tried not to eat dinner at night as much as I could. Whenever I failed to do so and ate something for dinner, that pain returned.”
